names.en: Shape and crumb stuffed rice balls

en: shape rice balls round a filling

does: Presses cold, firm risotto round a small piece of filling into a ball, a cone or an oval, and coats it in flour, beaten egg and crumbs in turn, so that it fries with a crisp shell around a soft, savoury middle.

intro.what: This arancini-style method encloses filling in firm risotto and coats the shape in crumbs.
intro.why: It teaches you to manage a soft filling inside a continuous rice wall and an even outer shell.

how: Cook the risotto a little firmer and thicker than for eating. Spread it out thin on a tray and let it cool right down, then chill it until it is stiff and holds together when pressed.
Have the filling cold and in small pieces. Set out shallow dishes in a row: flour, beaten egg and crumbs.
Wet the hands. Press a handful of rice into a hollow in the palm, set the filling in the middle, close the rice over it and turn it into the shape wanted, pressing out any crack or gap.
Roll it in the flour and shake off the extra, turn it through the egg, then roll it in the crumbs, pressing so that they cover it all round.
Lay them on a tray without touching and chill them for a short while before frying, so that the shell holds.

cues.text: Cold rice holds together when pressed and does not cling to wet hands.
Each ball is closed all round, with no filling showing and an even coat of crumbs.

mistakes.mistake: Shaping risotto that is warm or loose, which sticks to the hands and bursts in the oil.
mistakes.fix: Cook the risotto a little firmer, then cool it right down and chill it until it is stiff.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving a gap over the filling, through which it leaks out in the hot oil.
mistakes.fix: Close the rice all the way over the filling and press out any crack before the coat goes on.

mistakes.mistake: Packing in too much filling, so that the rice wall is thin and splits.
mistakes.fix: Use a small piece of filling and enough rice to wrap it with a firm wall all round.

quiz.question: What must the rice do around the filling?
choices: Leave a small opening for filling to escape.
Form a continuous wall without gaps.
Make a very thin patch only at the base.
quiz.because: A continuous rice enclosure supports the filling beneath the crumb shell.

quiz.question: What is the coating order?
quiz.because: Flour, egg and crumbs build the coating in stages so the shell covers the rice evenly.

quiz.question: Which feel suits rice before shaping?
choices: Cold and firm enough to hold when pressed.
Warm and loose between the fingers.
Fluid enough to run from the palm.
quiz.because: Firm chilled rice holds a wall around the filling instead of clinging and slumping.

quiz.question: The rice wall split around a large filling. What would you change when shaping the next ball?
choices: Stretch the same thin wall further.
Use less filling and enough rice to enclose it firmly.
Hide the exposed filling beneath loose crumbs.
quiz.because: Reducing the filling leaves enough rice to form an intact supporting wall.

comes_after.why: There is no risotto to shape until it has been cooked, then cooled and chilled.
The beaten-in butter and cheese make the rice cling together when it is cold.

variant_of.differs: The mixture is whole grains of cold risotto and not a smooth paste, and it is pressed round a piece of filling, which a croqueta does not have. The shell is the same flour, egg and crumbs.

The rice is risotto cooked in stock and chilled until stiff, and not plain warm rice, and it is wrapped round a filling and then coated in flour, egg and crumbs to be fried. Onigiri are plain rice pressed warm with salted hands and eaten as they are.
